title: Acridocarpus orientalis ethanolic extract induces senescence and abortive autophagy in human breast cancer cells
task: Evaluate anti-cancer activity of Acridocarpus orientalis extract against triple negative breast cancer
key_results: AOEE inhibited proliferation in concentration- and time-dependent manner; induced G1/S cell cycle arrest with upregulation of p21WAF1, p27Kip1 and downregulation of Cyclin D1, PCNA; induced p16-dependent senescence and abortive autophagy
comments: The induction of abortive autophagy (where autophagy machinery is activated but completion is blocked) is an interesting mechanism that may contribute to senescence rather than cell death.

hypotheses.hypothesis: AOEE induces cell cycle arrest through CDK inhibitor upregulation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed - p21WAF1 and p27Kip1 upregulated with concurrent Cyclin D1 and PCNA downregulation

hypotheses.hypothesis: AOEE induces senescence in TNBC cells
hypotheses.result: Confirmed - p16-dependent senescence induced in MDA-MB-231 cells with SA-β-gal expression

hypotheses.hypothesis: ERK and p38 pathways mediate autophagy and senescence induction
hypotheses.result: Supported - Both pathways activated upon AOEE treatment

title: NuSAP1 promotes spindle assembly in Trypanosoma brucei by bundling spindle microtubules
task: Characterize NuSAP1 function in spindle assembly and mitotic regulation in Trypanosoma brucei
key_results: NuSAP1 bundles microtubules in vitro; NuSAP1 depletion disrupts spindle assembly and kinetochore biorientation; NuSAP1 required for MAP103 and TbMlp2 spindle pole localization and spindle pole complex-nuclear basket association
comments: The unusual NuSAP-dependent spindle assembly mechanism in trypanosomes highlights divergent mitotic regulation strategies across eukaryotes and may reveal therapeutic targets specific to parasitic protozoans.

hypotheses.hypothesis: NuSAP1 directly bundles spindle microtubules to promote spindle assembly
hypotheses.result: Confirmed - NuSAP1 bundles microtubules in vitro; NuSAP1 depletion disrupts spindle assembly

hypotheses.hypothesis: NuSAP1 is required for spindle pole protein complex formation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed - NuSAP1 depletion disrupts MAP103 and TbMlp2 localization to spindle poles

hypotheses.hypothesis: NuSAP1 regulates stability and localization of NuSAP4 and SPB1
hypotheses.result: Confirmed - NuSAP1 interacts with NuSAP4 and SPB1; regulates their stability and localization

title: Automatic prediction of cotton leaf’s diseases using deep learning techniques
task: Automated classification of cotton leaf diseases using transfer learning
key_results: CLDP-CNN model achieved 99.78% accuracy on primary field dataset and 99.62% on secondary Kaggle dataset; VGG16 baseline achieved 99.56% on primary and 98.82% on secondary datasets
comments: Exceptionally high accuracies raise concerns about potential data leakage, dataset characteristics, or evaluation methodology that should be scrutinized before deployment.

inputs: Cotton leaf images from field farms and Kaggle
outputs: Disease classification (Bacterial Blight, Fusarium Wilt, Curl Virus Disease)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Transfer learning-based CLDP-CNN outperforms traditional deep learning for cotton leaf disease classification on real-world field images
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; CLDP-CNN achieved 99.78% on primary dataset, exceeding secondary dataset performance

title: Automated enhancement of post-infectious lung CT images using multi-technique noise detection and denoising with quantitative evaluation
task: Denoising post-infectious lung CT images for improved diagnostic clarity
key_results: Automated noise detection combined with BM3D denoising achieved significant improvements in PSNR, SSIM, and edge preservation across multiple noise detection methods (Blur Laplacian, Noise Entropy, Noise Power Spectrum Density, Wavelet Transform)
comments: While image quality metrics are reported, clinical validation on diagnostic accuracy for actual disease detection is absent, limiting translation to clinical practice.

model_io.model: Deep ensemble learning with BM3D denoising
outputs: Denoised CT images with quantified quality metrics (PSNR, SSIM, edge preservation index)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Automated noise detection followed by BM3D denoising improves CT image quality metrics compared to raw images
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; significant enhancement in image clarity and structural clarity demonstrated via PSNR, SSIM, and edge preservation

title: Improving arrhythmic risk prediction using cardiac magnetic resonance within deep learning in ischemic heart disease
task: Improving arrhythmic risk prediction in ischemic heart disease using LGE-CMR and machine learning
key_results: Scar entropy emerged as a strong arrhythmic predictor; DeepSurv showed superior cross-cohort generalization, outperforming Cox regression and Random Survival Forests in discriminating IHD patients at risk for arrhythmic events
comments: Multi-cohort validation and comparison of interpretability-accuracy tradeoffs strengthen the findings, though scar entropy's mechanistic role in arrhythmia remains unclear.

inputs: Clinical variables and LGE-CMR-derived features (scar burden, heterogeneity)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Non-linear machine learning models outperform Cox regression for arrhythmic risk stratification in IHD
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; DeepSurv demonstrated superior cross-cohort generalization; scar entropy identified as key predictor

hypotheses.hypothesis: Scar heterogeneity (entropy) is an important prognostic marker for arrhythmic events beyond conventional LVEF
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; scar entropy consistently emerged as strong predictor in all modeling approaches

title: Detection of underground objects from GPR data using a lightweight YOLO-based approach
task: Detect small subsurface objects in GPR radargrams
key_results: 5.7% mAP improvement and 5.9% F1-score improvement on Integrated Dataset; reduced inference time while maintaining accuracy
comments: GhostConv integration elegantly reduces computational burden for real-time deployment, though evaluation on only four GPR datasets limits cross-domain generalization claims.

model_io.model: YOLOv8n with GhostConv and C3Ghost modules
outputs: object detections with bounding boxes and confidence scores

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ghost block-based architecture reduces computation while maintaining detection performance
hypotheses.result: Achieved 5.7% mAP and 5.9% F1 improvements with reduced inference time

title: Reliable estimation of the confined compressive strength of FRP-confined circular concrete columns using an ANFIS-based model
task: Predict confined compressive strength of FRP-confined concrete columns
key_results: ANFIS model demonstrated superior predictive consistency and reduced scatter versus five analytical confinement models on 812 experimental samples
comments: Levenberg–Marquardt backpropagation with early stopping is standard practice; superior performance over analytical models is notable, though physical interpretability of the ANFIS structure is not discussed.

model_io.model: Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) trained with Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm

hypotheses.hypothesis: ANFIS can learn nonlinear confinement relationships better than analytical equations
hypotheses.result: ANFIS showed superior predictive consistency and reduced scatter across 812 test samples

title: Centrifugal pump analysis and prediction in cavitation using RapidMiner tool and machine learning algorithms
task: Predict cavitation onset in centrifugal pumps
key_results: Fine Tree algorithm achieved 96.1% accuracy; Naive Bayes 95.5%; maximum vapour volume fraction 0.9477 at impeller water-moving part
comments: CFD-ML hybrid approach is practical, though the feature engineering relies on a single ratio (NPSHa/NPSHr) which may limit generalizability to diverse pump designs.

model_io.model: Fine Tree and Naive Bayes classifiers

hypotheses.hypothesis: ML algorithms can predict cavitation status from CFD-derived NPSHa/NPSHr ratio
hypotheses.result: Fine Tree achieved 96.1% accuracy, confirming feasibility

title: Integrated continuous berth allocation with time-invariant specific quay crane assignment using a mixed-integer model and greedy genetic algorithm
task: Integrated continuous berth allocation with time-invariant quay crane assignment
key_results: Mixed-integer programming model + greedy genetic algorithm generated high-quality feasible schedules within practical computation times on real port data; repair mechanism provided most evident quality gain
comments: Explicitly tracking crane identities rather than just counts is a practical refinement; greedy initialization and repair mechanisms are well-motivated but computational complexity scaling is not thoroughly analyzed.

model_io.model: Mixed-integer programming model solved with greedy genetic algorithm

hypotheses.hypothesis: Greedy initialization and repair operations improve solution quality and stability
hypotheses.result: Ablation study confirmed both components contribute, with repair mechanism providing most evident gain
